_about: The one per-language table. The game's I18n module (apps/game/scripts/i18n.gd) reads it once at start into I18n.LANGUAGES, and the i18n tool (scripts/i18n/i18n_tool.py, PR L2) reads the same file, so the game, the picker and the gates never keep two lists (research: codex/localization-research at 520cad1, docs/research-2026-10/localization/DESIGN.md and PLAN.md, PR L1). The export carries it (both presets export all resources, .json files included; measured with --export-pack). Nothing else lists these facts. 'languages' is keyed by Godot locale code, in the picker's order (English, then the Latin-script names A to Z, then Cyrillic, then CJK; LANGUAGES.md, 'The language picker'). Game fields: 'name' is the picker name in the language itself, never translated; 'enabled' offers the language (in the picker and to the OS-locale resolver; only English until a language's PR turns it on); 'review' is 'machine' until native review stamps it, then 'reviewed' (D2, D8; the source language has none); 'machine_tag' is the short 'machine translation' tag shown in the language itself while it is unreviewed (PIPELINE.md, 'Honest labelling'; null where the research gives none yet); 'fallback_font' is the bundled CJK subset I18n chains behind the game's fonts only while that language is on (PR L4 added the files, Noto Sans subsets cut to decision D7's fixed common sets by scripts/i18n/i18n_tool.py fonts; DESIGN.md, 'Fonts'), null for the languages the game's own Roboto and Montserrat draw; 'reading_cps' is the reading speed in characters a second (Netflix's subtitle limits for en 20, es 17, ja 4, ko 12, zh-Hans 9, PIPELINE.md sources; null where not yet sourced, and the dialogue boxes keep English's speed for it); 'row_characters' is the most characters a dialogue row holds (42, DialogueBoxes.MAX_ROW_CHARACTERS) or null where rows run to the column width (CJK, DESIGN.md 'Per-script row limits'). The dialogue boxes start reading the last two in PR L7d. Tool fields: 'glossary' is the language's key in the glossary and style guides (i18n/glossary.json and i18n/style/, PR L5); 'script' picks the script guard; 'family' is the base language, and every file of a family with two or more files must be complete (Godot looks a message up in every loaded file of the same language, so a gap in zh_Hant shows zh_Hans text: DESIGN.md, 'A missing line falls back to its sibling file'); 'plural_forms' is the gettext header rule (CLDR, the same as Godot's core/string/locales.h); 'gender' names a row of 'gender_rules'; 'name_case' turns on the check that no case ending is glued to the name slot (Slavic languages decline names). A gender rule holds these case-insensitive regular expressions: 'forms' matches one word that shows a person's grammatical gender (past tense, agreeing adjective or participle, job noun), read across a whole clause; 'near_forms' (optional) one agreeing word too common as a modifier of things to read across a clause (Russian full adjectives, French -ie/-ise/-euse/-eux participles and adjectives), read only within the window around the name slot or a second-person pronoun; 'you' a second-person pronoun, 'first_person' a first-person subject pronoun (a clause with one is about the speaker, WOLF), 'first_forms' (optional) one word that is first person by its ending alone (Polish -łem/-łam: WOLF's own verbs, skipped unless the engineer speaks), 'pronouns' a gendered third-person pronoun (searched in running text, so CJK rules need no spaces); 'person_words' (optional) a gendered noun or honorific for a person (女の子, 小姐, 언니), searched in running text on any line where the engineer appears. A '(?!(?:...)$)' list at the head of a pattern names common nouns that end like a gendered form (puerta, стена, strona). 'extends' copies every field the row does not set from another row. Patterns are heuristics: a flag costs a look, a miss is caught by native review (PIPELINE.md, 'The engineer is never gendered').
